feedback: If a child gives directions from their own viewpoint so 'turn left' is wrong for the follower, do NOT treat it as a failure: walk the route exactly as they said so they SEE the mismatch, then model taking the follower's view. De-centring matures with age.
When a robot hits a wall, name whether the direction or the amount of turn was wrong and let the child re-string the instruction.
Probe with 'turn that quarter anti-clockwise this time — where do you face now?' to check the direction convention under a new turn.
Ask 'when you say turn left, is that your left or mine?' to surface the follower's frame of reference.
activities.intendedInsight: Direction and turn words are most useful when they form a sequence another person can follow from their own viewpoint — producing a followable route is the real goal.
learnerActions: Guide a partner (or a floor robot) from one point to another using a sequence such as 'forward 2, turn clockwise quarter, forward 3', combining straight-line moves with named turns.
Have the follower act out the route exactly as given, from the follower's own facing, and watch what happens.
On a grid, drive a programmable robot through a maze by stringing moves and turns; a wrong turn direction or wrong amount sends it into a wall, prompting a correction.
Play a barrier game: describe a route to someone who cannot see your map, using direction and turn words precisely enough for them to reproduce it.
When a route 'goes wrong', revise the instructions so the follower, not just you, can reach the target.
activities.title: Give and follow a multi-step route that someone else can act on

feedback: If a selection is wrong, re-make the turn physically and compare the finishing facing.
For a mismatched quarter-turn/right-angle pairing, mark the angle between start and finish arms and compare.
Treat recognition choices as a check only; always follow with giving or following a live route so the child constructs instructions, not just identifies them.
activities.intendedInsight: You can recognise correct turn facings and the quarter-turn/right-angle link quickly, then confirm sequences by acting them out.
learnerActions: After a stated clockwise or anti-clockwise quarter turn, pick which direction you now face from given options.
Match a quarter turn to one right angle, a half turn to two right angles, and a three-quarter turn to three right angles.
Put a jumbled set of move-and-turn instructions into the order that reaches a target, then test the order by walking or driving it.
activities.title: Check and sort turn and route language
